resolutions.finding: C1. R037 feature_notes: 'Claude, Codex and Gemini omit an empty env or headers object entirely' - critic says Gemini remote emits headers unconditionally.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPProviderConfig.swift:126-146 gemini(_:). The remote branch (:129-133) builds the entry as a single unconditional dictionary literal: entries[server.id] = .object(["httpUrl": .string(server.url ?? ""), "headers": .object(server.headers.mapValues(JSONValue.string))]). There is no `if !server.headers.isEmpty` guard, so a remote server with no headers still writes "headers": {}. Only the Gemini LOCAL branch guards env: :135-141 var entry = ["command":..., "args":...]; if !server.env.isEmpty { entry["env"] = ... }.
Exact per-provider emission, all four re-read in full:
  claude(_:) :4-28 -> root key "mcpServers". remote: {"type":"http","url":<url or "">} plus "headers" ONLY if non-empty (:12-14). local: {"command":<or "">,"args":[...]} plus "env" ONLY if non-empty (:21-23).
  codex(_:) :30-51 -> root key "mcp_servers". remote: {"url":<or "">} plus "http_headers" ONLY if non-empty (:35-37) - the key is http_headers, not headers. local: {"command","args"} plus "env" ONLY if non-empty (:44-46).
  copilot(_:) :53-75 -> root key "mcpServers". remote (:57-62): {"type":"http","url","headers" ALWAYS,"tools":["*"]}. local (:64-70): {"type":"local","command","args","env" ALWAYS,"tools":["*"]}.
  gemini(_:) :126-146 -> root key "mcpServers". remote (:130-133): {"httpUrl","headers" ALWAYS} and NO "type" key. local (:135-142): {"command","args"} plus "env" ONLY if non-empty.
Counting the always-emitted possibly-empty maps: copilot remote "headers", copilot local "env", gemini remote "headers" = 3 of the 8 branches. The other 5 guard.
Also: the missing-value fallback is the empty string, not omission - .string(server.url ?? "") and .string(server.command ?? "") at :10, :18, :34, :41, :59, :66, :131, :136.
R037 also contradicted itself, as the critic said: a persisted_fields line calling Gemini remote {httpUrl, headers} unconditional while the feature note called headers omitted.
resolutions.port_impact: gemini-settings.json must write "headers": {} for every remote server with no headers - which is every OAuth server, because MCPStore registers routes with headers: [:] and MCPResolvedServer.headers stays empty for the .oauth transport (MCP.swift:164-167 sets only url and oauthUpstream). copilot.json must likewise always carry "headers" on remote entries and "env" on local ones, plus "tools": ["*"] on both. claude.json and codex.json must omit those keys when empty. Do not normalize the four writers to one shape.

resolutions.finding: C2. R038: MCPStore.value(for:of:) is 'draft first, else the Keychain secret for a .secret field, else the connection's stored value, else field.defaultValue'.
resolutions.port_impact: The port's field-value reader must be a strict if/else-if on field kind, not a fallback chain. resolutions.finding: C3. R037 files the 240-second mcp-remote deadline as an open question while its own notes record mcp-remote is minted only by acpServers(allowsHTTP: false).
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Two facts settle it.
(a) MCPProbe.swift:115-116: let isOAuth = server.args.contains("mcp-remote") then let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(isOAuth ? 240 : 90). The 240 s deadline and the .unauthorizedOAuth stderr mapping (:218-224, fired when isOAuth && (stderr.contains("Unauthorized") || stderr.contains("invalid_grant"))) both hang off that one args check.
(b) A repo-wide grep for the literal "mcp-remote" in *.swift returns exactly 3 hits: MCPProbe.swift:115 (the consumer), MCPProviderConfig.swift:99 (the only producer - var args: [JSONValue] = [.string("-y"), .string("mcp-remote"), .string(url)] inside acpServers(allowsHTTP:) when allowsHTTP is false), and ACPSession.swift:253 (a comment).
acpServers(...)'s return value goes to exactly one place: ACPSession.swift:254, as the "mcpServers" field of session/new and session/load params. It never becomes an MCPResolvedServer and never reaches MCPProbe. MCPProbe's only caller is MCPStore.probeOnce (MCPStore.swift:313) via startProbe (:316-319), and both always pass entry.resolve(values: storedValues(for: entry)). Across the 33 catalog entries (MCPCatalog.swift:4-456), no .stdio args array contains "mcp-remote" - the stdio commands are npx/uvx with package names only.
Therefore, for every built-in catalog server isOAuth is ALWAYS false, the deadline is ALWAYS 90 s, and the stderr unauthorizedOAuth mapping never fires. The only reachable route in this checkout is a user-authored custom stdio server (MCPCustom.swift:93-118) whose args literally contain "mcp-remote".
resolutions.port_impact: Implement the branch exactly (args contains "mcp-remote" -> 240 s else 90 s; stderr scan for "Unauthorized" or "invalid_grant") but do not build a 240-second wait into the built-in-server experience. The OAuth retry the user actually sees comes from the HTTP path: MCPProbeError.unauthorizedOAuth raised at MCPProbe.swift:254 on a 401/403 through the proxy, caught at MCPStore.swift:323-333.

Because MCPStore.connect stores draft text by kind (MCPStore.swift:103-112: if field.kind == .secret { MCPKeychain.set(...) } else { connection.values[field.key] = text }), those three keys are the ONLY keys that can ever appear inside MCPConnection.values in mcp.json for a built-in server. postgres's and mongodb's connection strings never land in mcp.json.

MCPField's own defaults (MCP.swift:18-37): kind defaults to .secret, help nil, defaultValue nil, isRequired true. MCPField.Kind has exactly 3 cases: secret, text, path (MCP.swift:19-23).
Env maps declared on stdio entries: brave-search {"BRAVE_API_KEY":"{key}"} (:152), firecrawl {"FIRECRAWL_API_KEY":"{key}"} (:193), perplexity {"PERPLEXITY_API_KEY":"{key}"} (:210), slack {"SLACK_MCP_XOXB_TOKEN":"{token}","SLACK_MCP_ADD_MESSAGE_TOOL":"true"} (:227), mongodb {"MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING":"{url}"} (:409), aws-docs {"FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL":"ERROR"} (:452). Three built-in keys ("instance", "root", "path") go to the plaintext mcp.json values map; the other nine go to DPAPI/credential storage and must never be written to disk in the clear. A port that treats .path as secret breaks the filesystem and sqlite cards; one that treats postgres/mongodb "url" as text leaks a DSN into mcp.json.

  discoveryFailed(detail): detail.isEmpty ? "Couldn't find the sign-in page." : "Couldn't find the sign-in page. " + detail
  metadataFailed(detail): detail.isEmpty ? "The server's sign-in details didn't make sense." : "The server's sign-in details didn't make sense. " + detail
  registrationUnsupported: "This server doesn't let apps sign in on their own."

  tokenFailed(detail): detail.isEmpty ? "Couldn't finish signing in." : "Couldn't finish signing in. " + detail

  timedOut: "Sign-in timed out. Try again and complete it in the browser."
  cancelled: "Sign-in was cancelled."

Detail strings minted in this file: "That address doesn't look like a URL." (:201, :244, :804), "The authorization address isn't valid." (:147), "It's missing the addresses needed to sign in." (:335), "The server only signs in apps it has approved (403), so this one can't yet." (:384), "The server refused to set things up (<status>)." (:385), "The server didn't hand back a token." (:627), "The sign-in expired." (:666), "Couldn't listen for the sign-in reply." (:414, :425), "The connection to the browser broke." (:439), "The browser didn't send back a code." resolutions.finding: G4. Protected-resource metadata: scopes_supported not recorded, and only the FIRST element of authorization_servers is used.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPOAuth.discover(url:) :199-247 reads exactly three fields from the protected-resource metadata document, in both the challenge-directed branch (:208-215) and the well-known-probe branch (:224-235):
  issuer = json["authorization_servers"]?.array?.first?.string   -- FIRST element only, the rest ignored (:209, :228)
  resource = json["resource"]?.string                            (:210, :229)
  resourceScopes = json["scopes_supported"]?.array -> compactMap(\.string).filter { !$0.isEmpty }; nil when that list is empty (:211-214, :230-233)
The probe branch additionally requires the document to carry at least one of the two: guard hasServers || hasResource else { continue } (:225-227), where hasServers checks only that authorization_servers is an array and hasResource that resource is a string. Probe candidates, in order (:219-222): <origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource<path> then <origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, where path is requestURL.path.
If resourceScopes is still nil, it falls back to the WWW-Authenticate challenge's scope parameter, space-split (:238-240, :304-308).
Issuer fallback: (issuer ?? origin(of: url)) then trimmed of leading AND trailing "/" via trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "/")) (:241-245).
Where resourceScopes then lands, both places: the dynamic-registration body's "scope" key, space-joined (:374-376), and the authorization URL's scope query item, space-joined (:593-595). resource lands in the authorization URL as a resource query item (:590-592), in the code-exchange form body (:618-620), in the refresh form body (:657-659), and is persisted as "resource" in the Keychain session (:705-707).
Authorization-server metadata (fetchAuthorizationServerMetadata :310-351) reads exactly three fields: authorization_endpoint (required, non-empty), token_endpoint (required, non-empty), registration_endpoint (optional). Candidate order (:312-325): when the issuer has a non-empty path other than "/", first <origin>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server<path> and <origin>/.well-known/openid-configuration<path>; then always <issuer>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration. Up to 4 candidates, tried in order, first success wins; on exhaustion it throws metadataFailed(lastError).
WWW-Authenticate parsing (:249-308): a 401 from a plain GET of the MCP URL is required (:254-257); every WWW-Authenticate header value is collected case-insensitively, String or [String] (:258-268); challengeParameter (:290-302) finds <name>= and takes either a double-quoted value or a bare run up to the next comma or space, returning nil when empty. The two parameters read are "resource_metadata" (:284-286) and "scope" (:304-308). The source comment at :288-289 says Stripe sends resource_metadata bare.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must read scopes_supported and thread it into both the registration scope and the authorize scope; must use only authorization_servers[0]; must keep the 2-candidate protected-resource probe order and the up-to-4-candidate authorization-server metadata order; and must accept a bare (unquoted) resource_metadata parameter.

resolutions.finding: G5. Probe reads server name and version from result.serverInfo.{name,version}; no report named the serverInfo object.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Stdio path, MCPProbe.swift:194-197: let initResult = initReply["result"]; guard initResult?.object != nil else { throw MCPProbeError.malformed("missing result") }; let serverName = initResult?["serverInfo"]?["name"]?.string; let serverVersion = initResult?["serverInfo"]?["version"]?.string. The value persists as MCPConnection.serverVersion (MCP.swift:195) via MCPStore.swift:337 connection.serverVersion = result.serverVersion. MCPProbeResult.serverName (MCP.swift:181) is carried but MCPStore never stores it - only serverVersion and tools are written.
The initialize params the probe sends (:65-71) are exactly {"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"Droppy Code","version":"1.0"}}. The request envelope (:73-81) is {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<int>,"method":<string>[,"params":<value>]}; a notification (:83-85) is {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":<string>} with NO id and NO params.

  MCPHub.swift:279-283: throw MCPHubError.server(error["message"]?.string ?? "unknown error"). MCPHubError.server renders the message ALONE (case .server(let message): return message, :11-12), so the user sees exactly "unknown error" with no prefix. The "The server sent something unexpected: " prefix IS hard-coded into four separate MCPHub literals, which is the likely source of the confusion: "The server sent something unexpected: missing result." (MCPHub.swift:379 stdio init, :434 http init), "The server sent something unexpected: empty reply." (:430, :448) and "The server sent something unexpected: invalid reply." (:466).
Other MCPProbeError.malformed details, all MCPProbe.swift: "missing command or URL" (:60), "missing result" (:195, :276), "invalid URL" (:241), "empty reply" (:268), "invalid reply" (:270, :319).
Other MCPHubError.server literals: "The server quit." (:301, :312, :317, :409), "The server quit (exit <code>)." (:405), "The server didn't answer in time." (:413), "<command> isn't installed." (:326), "The server address is invalid." (:423), "The server answered <status>." (:470). MCPHubError.unknownTool renders "Unknown tool: <callName>." (:9-10).
Full MCPProbeError.errorDescription table (MCPProbe.swift:16-48): commandMissing("npx") -> "npx isn't installed. Install Node.js from nodejs.org, then try again."; commandMissing("uvx") -> "uvx isn't installed. Run `brew install uv` in Terminal, then try again."; commandMissing(other) -> "<name> isn't installed. Install it, then try again."; exited -> "The server quit (exit <code>). <last non-empty trimmed stderr line>" or "The server quit (exit <code>)." when stderr has none; timedOut -> "The server didn't answer in time."; http 401/403 -> "That key was refused. resolutions.finding: G7. MCPProbe.postJSON uses a 30-second URLRequest timeout for every remote probe request; absent from the timeout notes.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPProbe.swift:308: var request = URLRequest(url: url, timeoutInterval: 30) - a flat 30 s for every remote probe request (initialize, notifications/initialized, and each tools/list page). Full MCP timeout table, re-read:
  MCPProbe stdio: deadline = now + 240 s when args contain "mcp-remote", else now + 90 s (:116); reply poll interval 5 ms (try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(5)), :188); terminate() sends SIGTERM then, 1 second later on a .utility global queue, SIGKILL to -pid when the process leads its own group else to pid (:226-235).
  MCPProbe remote: 30 s per HTTP request (:308).
  MCPHub stdio: reply poll interval 10 ms (:415); initialize wait 60 s (:377); listTools rpc timeout 60 s (:198); callTool rpc timeout 120 s (:227); same SIGTERM-then-1s-SIGKILL terminate (:285-294).
  MCPHub http: the per-call timeout IS threaded into the request - URLRequest(url: url, timeoutInterval: timeout) (:455) - so initialize uses 60 s (:428), the notifications/initialized post uses 30 s (:439), tools/list 60 s and tools/call 120 s (:446).
  MCPProxy upstream: request.timeoutInterval = 3_600 (MCPProxy.swift:325).
  MCPOAuth: every URLRequest is timeoutInterval: 30 (:251, :720, :749, :773); the browser callback listener deadline is callbackTimeout = 300 s (:129, :451-453).
  MCPBridge (JS): CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000, applied by Promise.race per server in loadMCPTools (MCPBridgeSource.swift:17, :50-56, :225, :227); fetch itself is unbounded.
resolutions.port_impact: Seven distinct timeout regimes. Do not unify them. Most importantly the probe's remote leg is 30 s flat while the hub's remote leg varies 30/60/120, and the proxy holds an hour-long upstream request so streamable-HTTP SSE sessions survive.

resolutions.finding: G8. The proxy-port file is written as a side effect of the first read of MCPProxy.port, and that first read happens inside MCPCatalogEntry.resolve.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. The side effect is real; the claim about which call triggers it first is WRONG for this checkout.
Side effect: MCPProxy.swift:14 private static let portBox = Mutex<UInt16>(loadPort()). Swift static stored properties are lazily initialized on first access, so loadPort() (:17-25) runs the first time anything reads MCPProxy.port (:12). loadPort reads <MCPPaths.directory>/proxy-port (:15) as UTF-8, accepts a trimmed UInt16 != 0, and OTHERWISE calls pickFreePort() and immediately WRITES the picked value back with try? "\(picked)".write(to: portFile, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8) (:22-24). Reading a property writes a file.
Ordering: MCPProxy.port is read in exactly two places in the whole repo - MCPProxy.start() line 90 (listen(on: Self.port, canRepick: true)) and MCP.swift:165 (MCPProxy.url(for: id) inside MCPCatalogEntry.resolve's .oauth case, via MCPProxy.url :35-37). MCPStore.init (MCPStore.swift:22-28) runs load(), then MCPProxy.shared.start() (:26), then exportAll() (:28); exportAll is the first thing that touches enabledServers (:41-49) and therefore resolve. MCPStore() is constructed at exactly one site, AppModel.swift:123. So start() ALWAYS reads the port before any resolve() does, and the file write happens inside start(), not inside resolve().
pickFreePort (:159-175) binds a real AF_INET SOCK_STREAM socket to 127.0.0.1:0, reads back the kernel's choice with getsockname, closes it, and returns the literal 48123 on any failure or a zero result. MCPProxy.url(for:) returns exactly "http://127.0.0.1:\(port)/mcp/\(serverID)".
resolutions.port_impact: The port must still make the port lazy and self-persisting, because resolve() is a legal second trigger and because the ordering guarantee rests only on MCPStore.init's statement order. Reproduce the 48123 fallback and the exact route URL shape. The Windows equivalent of bind-0-then-getsockname is the same; do not substitute a hard-coded default port.

resolutions.finding: G9. repickPort() moves the port and rewrites proxy-port, but nothing re-runs MCPProviderConfig.writeAll, so configs written this launch point at the dead port.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, and an upstream defect. MCPStore.init (MCPStore.swift:22-28) calls MCPProxy.shared.start() then exportAll(). start() (MCPProxy.swift:82-91) sets running = true and calls listen(on: Self.port, canRepick: true), which builds the NWListener and calls listener.start(queue: queue) (:139) - asynchronous. exportAll() (:279-290) then runs synchronously and bakes http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp/<id> (via resolve -> MCPProxy.url) into claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json and gemini-settings.json through MCPProviderConfig.writeAll (:286).
Only LATER does the listener's stateUpdateHandler see .failed (MCPProxy.swift:118-131), cancel the listener, and - if canRepick - call self.listen(on: Self.repickPort(), canRepick: false). repickPort (:28-33) mutates portBox and rewrites the proxy-port file. Repo grep confirms MCPProviderConfig.writeAll has exactly one call site, MCPStore.exportAll (MCPStore.swift:286), and repickPort has exactly one call site, MCPProxy.swift:126. Nothing in the repick path calls back into MCPStore.
So every provider config written at launch keeps the old, dead port until the next exportAll - which only fires on disconnect (:133), setEnabled (:148), saveCustom when a connection existed (:187), or a successful probe (:343). Until then, any agent launched this session reaches a port nothing is listening on.
Second-order: the proxy-port FILE now holds the new port, so the NEXT launch is consistent; the damage is confined to the launch in which the repick happened. The source comment at MCPProxy.swift:8-11 explains the repick exists because a Dev build runs over a mirror of the release library and both would otherwise claim the same saved port.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the behavior, not a fix: the Windows port must not re-export configs on repick, or agents will see a different file than Droppy writes. Record it as a known defect. On Windows the same collision arises when two builds share %LOCALAPPDATA%\<AppName>\mcp\proxy-port.

resolutions.finding: G10. MCPBridgeSource never kills a spawned child; a hung server leaks a process for the host's lifetime.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPBridgeSource.swift contains ZERO occurrences of "kill", "unref" or "SIGTERM" (grep over the whole 252-line file returns nothing). connectStdio (:76-152) spawns with stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "ignore"] (:82) and installs handlers for child "error" and "exit" (:99-100) plus a stdin error swallow (:101), but no teardown. withTimeout (:50-56) only races the promise against setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("timed out")), CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS) with CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 (:17); its .finally clears the timer, nothing else. loadMCPTools (:218-234) catches and logs "droppy mcp: skipping " + server + ": " + errorText(error) to console.error (:230) and moves on. The spawned child survives.
This is the exact opposite of MCPHub, which registers every child in MCPLiveProcesses via MCPHub.track (MCPHub.swift:25, :370) and terminates the lot from AppDelegate.swift:54 MCPHub.terminateAll() - SIGTERM to all, then SIGKILL to any still running, to -pid for a group leader (MCPHub.swift:544-552). MCPProbe also cleans up (MCPProbe.swift:161-166 defer -> terminate).
Note loadMCPTools is strictly SEQUENTIAL (for ... of Object.keys(servers) with await inside, :221-232), so each hung server costs a full 15 s of startup before the next is tried.
resolutions.port_impact: Faithfully reproduce: the bridge .mjs must not kill children. On Windows the leak is worse than on macOS - an orphaned npx/node child of a Pi or Command Code host keeps running until the user kills it in Task Manager, and no process-group kill is applied. Record as an upstream defect; do not add a kill.

resolutions.finding: G11. The bridge's postMessage omits MCP-Protocol-Version, which MCPHub and MCPProbe both send.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPBridgeSource.swift:154-157: const requestHeaders = { ...(headers || {}), "Content-Type": "application/json", Accept: "application/json, text/event-stream" }; then if (sessionId) requestHeaders["mcp-session-id"] = sessionId;. That is the complete header set - Content-Type, Accept and a LOWERCASE mcp-session-id, on top of whatever the config's own headers carried. No MCP-Protocol-Version.
By contrast MCPHub.post sets it explicitly: urlRequest.setValue("2025-06-18", forHTTPHeaderField: "MCP-Protocol-Version") (MCPHub.swift:461), with Mcp-Session-Id in canonical casing (:462); MCPProbe.postJSON does the same (MCPProbe.swift:314-315).
Two further divergences the critic did not name:
  (i) the bridge's initialize clientInfo has NO version - clientInfo: { name: "Droppy Code" } (MCPBridgeSource.swift:138, :203) - whereas MCPHub (:261) and MCPProbe (:69) both send {"name":"Droppy Code","version":"1.0"}. PROTOCOL_VERSION is the same "2025-06-18" in all three (MCPBridgeSource.swift:16, MCPHub.swift:259, MCPProbe.swift:67).
  (ii) the bridge's SSE reader accepts a frame only when the parsed object has "result" or "error" in it (:170) and skips a data: payload of "[DONE]" (:167), while the Swift readers accept any object that has an "id" key (MCPHub.swift:486-488, MCPProbe.swift:341-343).
A third: the bridge sends notifications/initialized as an HTTP POST and swallows any failure (:195-202, :204), matching MCPHub :438-442 and MCPProbe :280-284 in spirit but not in header set.
resolutions.port_impact: The bridge .mjs is shipped text; copy it character for character, including the missing MCP-Protocol-Version, the lowercase mcp-session-id, the version-less clientInfo and the result/error-keyed SSE acceptance. A port that normalizes the three clients to one header set changes what remote MCP servers see from Pi and Command Code sessions.

resolutions.finding: G12. The proxy forwards the client's HTTP method verbatim (so GET and DELETE pass through) and copies back only three response headers, dropping WWW-Authenticate on a 401.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Method: MCPProxy.swift:324 request.httpMethod = method, where method comes straight from the request line parsed by parseHead (:220-236, which requires exactly 3 space-separated parts and a non-empty method and path). There is no method allowlist anywhere in the file, so GET (the streamable-HTTP SSE channel), DELETE (session teardown), POST and anything else are all relayed.
Request headers forwarded: exactly 5, by a fixed lowercase-to-canonical table (:326-337): content-type -> Content-Type, accept -> Accept, mcp-session-id -> Mcp-Session-Id, mcp-protocol-version -> MCP-Protocol-Version, last-event-id -> Last-Event-ID. Every other client header is dropped. Then route.headers are applied (:338-340) and, for an OAuth route, Authorization: Bearer <token> (:341-350).
Response headers copied back: exactly 3 (writeBack, :369-380) - Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id, Cache-Control. WWW-Authenticate is NOT among them, so a 401 reaches the client bare. Plus, per branch: for text/event-stream, Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Connection: close (:383-384); otherwise Content-Length: <n> and Connection: close (:403-404).
Routing (:284-303): the path is cut at the first "?"; it must start with "/mcp/"; the remainder must be non-empty and contain no "/"; and a route must exist. Every failure answers 502 with body {"error":"unknown server"} - deliberately never 404, per the comment at :286-287, because the app reads a 404 seen through the proxy as GitLab's own "MCP is off" answer.
Status reason phrases come from a fixed table of 12 named cases (:443-460): 200 OK, 201 Created, 202 Accepted, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found, 405 Method Not Allowed, 411 Length Required, 413 Content Too Large, 500 Internal Server Error, 502 Bad Gateway - with a default of "OK" for any other 2xx and "Error" otherwise.
resolutions.port_impact: Relay any method. Forward exactly those 5 request headers and copy back exactly those 3 response headers plus the per-branch framing headers. Answer 502 (never 404) for an unknown route. Reproduce the 12-case reason-phrase table and the 2xx/other default. Accept that OAuth discovery cannot work through a proxy route, because the challenge header is stripped.

resolutions.finding: G13. readBody on an early EOF forwards a truncated body upstream instead of refusing it.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPProxy.readBody :260-282. In the receive completion handler: if next.count >= need it routes the first need bytes (:274-275); else if isComplete || error != nil it calls routeRequest with next - whatever arrived - and no error (:276-277); otherwise it recurses (:279). So a client that declares Content-Length: 5000 and closes after 12 bytes has those 12 bytes POSTed upstream. There is no 400 and no length check on the relay path.
The refusals that DO exist, all in handleExchange (:238-258) and readHead (:191-218): 400 {"error":"bad request"} when parseHead returns nil (:239-241); 411 {"error":"chunked request bodies are not supported"} when transfer-encoding contains "chunked", case-insensitively (:243-247); 413 {"error":"request body too large"} when Content-Length exceeds bodyLimit = 32 * 1_024 * 1_024 = 33554432 (:50, :249-252); 413 {"error":"request head too large"} when the head exceeds headLimit = 65_536 before the CRLFCRLF divider (:49, :207-210). A missing or unparseable Content-Length becomes 0 via max(0, clientHeaders["content-length"].flatMap(Int.init) ?? 0) (:248), so such a request is relayed with an empty body.
jsonError (:462-469) escapes backslash, double quote, newline and carriage return, in that order, into {"error":"<message>"}.
The head is parsed with String(data:encoding:.isoLatin1) (:221), so any byte sequence decodes and header values are Latin-1, not UTF-8.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the silent truncation. The port must not add a 400 for short bodies. Reproduce the four refusals with their exact status codes and exact JSON bodies, the max(0, ...) Content-Length parse, and the Latin-1 head decode.

resolutions.finding: G14. MCPHub's `failed` set is consulted only by tools(); call() never checks it. The didRestart/dead policy is stdio-only.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, three separate points.
(a) failed: Set<String> (MCPHub.swift:48) is written in exactly one place - tools() at :68 after listTools throws, immediately followed by await client.stop() (:69) - and read in exactly one place, if failed.contains(id) { continue } (:59). call() (:78-97) never mentions it. call() checks only that the callName parses (:80), that a spec exists for that server (:81), and, WHEN a toolCache entry exists for that server, that the tool name is in it (:83-86). A server that failed listTools has NO toolCache entry, so that guard is skipped and self.client(for:spec:) (:87) hands back a live client that will start the process again on the next tool call.
(b) The one-restart policy lives entirely in ensureStdio (:311-322): if dead { throw }; return early if the process is running and initialized; if a process object exists but is not usable, throw and set dead when didRestart is already true, else set didRestart = true and start again. httpRPC (:421-452) has no dead, no didRestart and no restart concept at all - it only checks if !initialized and runs the initialize handshake inline.
(c) initialized is set true at :384 (stdio) and :437 (http) and cleared in exactly one place, stop() (:187). stop() is called from tools()'s catch (:69), from reload() for every existing client (:105) and from startStdio's own catch (:386). Nothing else clears it, so an HTTP client whose session the server has since dropped keeps believing it is initialized until reload().
reload() (:99-106) clears clients, toolCache, failed and specs and stops each old client on a detached Task; it is called from MCPStore.exportAll (MCPStore.swift:289).
Supporting detail: MCPHub.tools() sorts by server then name (:72-75); tool call names are "mcp__" + server + "__" + name (:37) and parse() splits on the FIRST "__" after the prefix (:108-116). Tool descriptions are truncated to 400 characters (:212) and a missing or non-object inputSchema becomes {"type":"object","properties":{}} (:203-208). callTool renders content items as text, "[image]" for type "image", and "[resource: <uri>]" for type "resource", joined by "\n" (:231-239), with isError from result.isError defaulting false (:242). readSpecs (:125-148) reads claude.json's mcpServers and prefers a non-empty command (stdio) over url (http); an entry with neither is skipped.
resolutions.port_impact: Scope the restart policy to stdio only. Do not add a failed-set check to call(). Do not clear initialized anywhere but stop(). These asymmetries are observable: a server that fails listTools disappears from the tool list yet is relaunched by a direct call.

resolutions.finding: G15. On probe success, connectedAt/serverVersion/tools are written only if a connection row exists, while states[] is set unconditionally.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPStore.startProbe success path, :334-343:
  try Task.checkCancellation()
  if var connection = connections[entry.id] {
      connection.connectedAt = .now
      connection.serverVersion = result.serverVersion
      connection.tools = result.tools
      connections[entry.id] = connection
  }
  states[entry.id] = .connected(toolCount: result.tools.count)
  save()
  exportAll()
The three connection fields are inside the if-var (:335-340); states[...] = .connected is outside it (:341). enabledServers filters on $0.isEnabled && $0.connectedAt != nil (:43), so a server with no connection row shows the connected pill and a tool count in the UI while reaching no provider config at all - and save() persists nothing for it, so the state is lost on relaunch (load() only revives states from stored connections, :254-259).
In the ordinary flow this cannot happen, because connect() writes connections[entry.id] = connection at :113 before startProbe at :117. The reachable path is refresh(_:) (:137-141), which calls startProbe directly with no write; if the row was removed in between (disconnect sets connections[id] = nil at :129), the probe's success lands in the gap. saveCustom (:180-188) also clears connectedAt on an existing row without removing it, so that path stays consistent.
The failure paths for comparison (:344-353): CancellationError is swallowed entirely; MCPProbeError.needsSetup(guide) sets states[id] = .needsSetup(guide) and deliberately KEEPS the sign-in so "Check again" re-probes without another browser round trip (comment at :347-348); any other error sets states[id] = .failed(message: error.localizedDescription). None of these three writes the connection or calls save()/exportAll().
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the guard exactly - do not hoist the three writes out of the conditional and do not move the states[] write inside it. The divergence between the connected badge and enabledServers is upstream behavior.

resolutions.finding: G16. MCPKeychain.set's SecItemUpdate query carries no kSecAttrAccessible; only the SecItemAdd fallback applies kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPKeychain.swift:30-50. The query (:37-41) is exactly three attributes: kSecClass = kSecClassGenericPassword, kSecAttrService = AppInfo.name, kSecAttrAccount = account(server:field:). SecItemUpdate(query, [kSecValueData: data]) (:42) updates only the data; if it returns errSecSuccess the function returns true immediately (:43) and the item keeps whatever accessibility it was created with. Only when the update returns errSecItemNotFound (:44) does it merge kSecValueData AND kSecAttrAccessible: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked and call SecItemAdd (:45-49). Any other OSStatus returns false.
The account name format is "MCP " + server + " " + field (:7-9) - the literal "MCP", a space, the catalog id, a space, the field key. The service is AppInfo.name. So the OAuth session for gitlab is account "MCP gitlab oauth" and its registered client is "MCP gitlab oauth-client" (MCPOAuth.swift:164, :185, :189-190, :356, :396, :711).
Read side (:11-26): returns nil unconditionally under CaptureRun (:12), then requires errSecSuccess, Data, valid UTF-8, and a non-empty value after trimming whitespace and newlines; the returned string is the TRIMMED one (:25). Write side trims first and, for an empty trimmed value, DELETES the item and returns true (:31-35). deleteAll(server entry:) iterates entry.fields only (:63-67) - so it does NOT remove the "oauth" and "oauth-client" items, which are removed separately by MCPOAuth.signOut (MCPOAuth.swift:188-191), called from MCPStore.disconnect :125-128 and from the two re-sign-in guards at :94 and :100 and the two probe-retry paths at :325 and :330.
resolutions.port_impact: On Windows the DPAPI/credential-store equivalent has no accessibility attribute, so the attribute itself has no analogue - but the port must reproduce the update-then-add shape, the trimming rules and the empty-value-deletes-the-item behavior, and must keep the exact account string "MCP <serverID> <fieldKey>" plus the two reserved field names "oauth" and "oauth-client", since those names are the persisted keys.

resolutions.finding: G17. Unreachable/dead code nobody classified: (a) MCPProxy.stop(), (b) MCPOAuth.refreshIfNeeded, (c) MCPProxy.Route.headers always empty, (d) MCPProbe's isOAuth branch.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, all four verified by repo-wide grep over *.swift.

Proof: grepping every MCPProxy. reference outside MCPProxy.swift yields exactly 9 hits (MCP.swift:165 url; MCPStore.swift:26 start, :282 replaceAll, :311 register, :95 :101 :127 :326 :331 unregister) and none is stop; grepping .stop() repo-wide hits only ThreadRuntime.swift:1473 :1542 :2054, MCPHub.swift:69 and :105 (MCPClient.stop), ACPSession.swift:243 and SettleChime.swift:19. (b) MCPOAuth.refreshIfNeeded(serverID:) (MCPOAuth.swift:193-195) has ZERO call sites. The only other refreshIfNeeded hits in the repo are TokenLedger.swift:157 and its caller TokenActivitySection.swift:97, an unrelated API. It should keep Route.headers in the data model (the type exists) while knowing nothing populates it. resolutions.finding: G18. The OAuth callback listener sets requiredLocalEndpoint but not requiredInterfaceType = .loopback, unlike MCPProxy.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPOAuth.runCallbackServer :408-415:
  let parameters = NWParameters.tcp
  parameters.requiredLocalEndpoint = NWEndpoint.hostPort(host: "127.0.0.1", port: .any)
  ... NWListener(using: parameters)
That is the entire parameter setup - no requiredInterfaceType, no allowLocalEndpointReuse. MCPProxy.listen sets all three (:100-103): parameters.requiredInterfaceType = .loopback, parameters.allowLocalEndpointReuse = true, parameters.requiredLocalEndpoint = .hostPort(host: "127.0.0.1", port: endpointPort), and its comment (:93-97) records that naming the port a SECOND time via NWListener(using:on:) is rejected with EINVAL, which left the proxy silent and every OAuth server unreachable.
In practice the callback listener still binds loopback-only because the required local endpoint pins 127.0.0.1; the missing interface-type restriction is a belt-without-braces difference. The redirect URI is built from the kernel-assigned port: "http://127.0.0.1:\(port)/callback" (:428).
The listener is cancelled by CallbackWait.finish (:111-118) on the first outcome and by the withTaskCancellationHandler onCancel (:455-457). The 300 s timeout is armed with queue.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + callbackTimeout) (:451-453) and fires MCPOAuthError.timedOut. The listener's .failed state yields network("The connection to the browser broke.") and .cancelled yields MCPOAuthError.cancelled (:438-441).
Request handling (:497-561): only GET is accepted (405 otherwise); only "/callback" or a "/callback?..." target is accepted (404 otherwise); the head is read until CRLFCRLF with a 1 MiB cap (:478-484, 1024*1024); query is parsed by prefixing "http://127.0.0.1" (:525). Outcome order: provider error first (:529-537), then missing or empty code (:538-544), then a state mismatch against the expected value (:545-551), then success (:552-560). The branded page is sent BEFORE the continuation resumes in every case.
Randomness: the PKCE verifier is 32 random bytes base64url-encoded, the state is 24 random bytes base64url-encoded (:135-137, :815-833), and the challenge is base64url(SHA256(verifier)) with code_challenge_method "S256" (:586-587, :823-826). randomToken fills bytes with UInt8.random(in: UInt8.min...UInt8.max) - Swift's system RNG, per byte, NOT SecRandomCopyBytes. base64url is standard base64 with + -> -, / -> _, and = stripped (:828-833).
resolutions.port_impact: Bind the Windows callback listener to 127.0.0.1 with an OS-assigned port and no interface-type constraint, matching the source. Reproduce the 300 s timeout, the GET-only and /callback-only checks, the 1 MiB head cap, the outcome order, the send-page-then-resume ordering, and the 32/24-byte token sizes with S256 PKCE.

resolutions.finding: T1. R037's MCPOAuth.swift entry is thin for a 929-line file: paraphrases the SVG, omits the base+detail rule, omits scopes_supported, omits that expires_at is optional, omits the missing interface restriction.

resolutions.finding: X5. The env var carrying the bridge path is never named: DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Two setters, both with the same two-step shape:
  PiSession.swift:105-110: if let bridge = try? MCPBridge.installBridge() { environment["DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE"] = bridge.path } then if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path) { environment["DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG"] = MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path }.
  CommandCodeSession.swift:174-179: the identical two blocks.
DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG is set ONLY when claude.json EXISTS on disk - a file-existence check, not the non-empty-mcpServers check the CLI flags use. So an empty-but-present claude.json still sets the variable, and the bridge then reads it and registers nothing.
Two consumers read the bridge variable: PiCLI.swift:169 const bridge = process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE ? await import(process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE) : null; and CommandCodeAPI.swift:388 const bridgePath = process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE. The bridge itself reads the config variable: MCPBridgeSource.swift:21 const file = process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG || ""; returning {} when unset (:22) or on any read/parse error, logging "droppy mcp: could not read config: " + errorText(error) (:25-28).
PiSession also sets DROPPY_CODE_PI_GATE and PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK = "1" (:103-104); CommandCodeSession sets or clears DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS (:169-173).
resolutions.port_impact: Both variable names are persisted contract with shipped JavaScript and must keep the DROPPY_CODE_ prefix exactly. On Windows the bridge path must be something Node's dynamic import accepts - a bare drive-letter path fails ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME in await import(...), so the port must hand Pi and Command Code a file:// URL or an otherwise importable path. That is a genuine porting decision, not a parity break, because the macOS POSIX path works as-is.

resolutions.finding: X6. MCPHub's only consumer, left unresolved.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Repo-wide grep for MCPHub outside MCPHub.swift gives exactly five hits:
  OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:510: if withTools, !didLoadMCPTools { mcpTools = await MCPHub.shared.tools(); didLoadMCPTools = true }
  OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:898: if let (server, name) = MCPHub.parse(callName: tool.name) { ... } - the nonisolated static parser, used to recognise an MCP call, title the tool event "<server> \u{00B7} <name>" (MIDDLE DOT) and gate an approval titled "Call <server> <name>"
  OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:904: let result = try await MCPHub.shared.call(tool.name, arguments: args)
  MCPStore.swift:289: Task { await MCPHub.shared.reload() } inside exportAll
  AppDelegate.swift:54: MCPHub.terminateAll()
So MCPHub serves exactly one provider family - the in-app OpenAI-compatible model-API sessions - and nothing else. A failed MCP call there returns "Error: the MCP tool reported failure with no output." when the result text is empty (:908), and tool output is summarized to a 12000-character limit (:910).
resolutions.port_impact: Scope the hub to the in-app model-API provider only. Its lifetime hook is the app-quit terminateAll; wire the port's equivalent to the same quit path so no npx/node child survives the app.

resolutions.finding: X7. Token expiry mis-stated as unconditional; and the proxy's 401 replay is a byte-identical retry when expires_at is absent.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, both halves.
(a) storeSession (MCPOAuth.swift:681-712) writes expires_at ONLY when the token response carried expires_in: if let expiresIn { session["expires_at"] = Date().timeIntervalSince1970 + Double(expiresIn) } (:699-701). expiresIn comes from json["expires_in"]?.int at both call sites (:633 code exchange, :672 refresh). A provider that omits expires_in leaves no expires_at in the stored session.
(b) accessToken (:163-182): let needsRefresh: Bool = { guard let expiresAt = json["expires_at"]?.double else { return false }; return Date().timeIntervalSince1970 >= expiresAt - 90 }() then guard needsRefresh else { return accessToken } (:171-175). A missing expires_at means needsRefresh == false forever - the session NEVER refreshes proactively. The refresh window is 90 seconds before expiry. A session that does need refreshing but has no non-empty refresh_token throws MCPOAuthError.signedOut (:176-178).
(c) MCPProxy.sendUpstream (:341-362): the first call sets Bearer <accessToken(serverID:)>; if the route uses OAuth and the response is 401, it calls try? await MCPOAuth.accessToken(serverID: serverID) AGAIN (:357) and, on success, replays the same request with the returned token. accessToken is the same function - it does not force a refresh, it re-reads the Keychain and applies the same expiry test. So with no expires_at the second call returns the identical cached token and the replay is byte-identical: same request, same Authorization header, one extra round trip, same 401.
(d) The only thing that DOES clear a bad token is the probe path: MCPProbe raises .unauthorizedOAuth on a 401/403 through the proxy (MCPProbe.swift:250-254) and MCPStore.startProbe catches it, calls MCPOAuth.signOut and MCPProxy.unregister, and re-runs probeOnce, which re-runs the full browser sign-in (MCPStore.swift:323-333, :307-313). A raw MCPProbeError.http(401 or 403) with an oauthUpstream is handled the same way (:328-332).
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce all of it, including the useless replay. Do not add a force-refresh parameter to the token getter and do not synthesize an expires_at when the provider omits expires_in. The 90-second pre-expiry window and the single-flight gate keyed by serverID must both be present.

resolutions.finding: X8. Custom-server migration risk: Variable's synthesized decoder has no default for isSecret, and one bad variable drops EVERY custom server.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPCustomServer.Variable (MCPCustom.swift:15-19) is struct Variable: Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable { var key: String; var isSecret = false; var id: String { key } } with NO custom init(from:). Swift's synthesized decoder does not consult a property's default value - it emits decode(Bool.self, forKey: .isSecret), which throws DecodingError.keyNotFound when the key is absent. (Optional-typed properties get decodeIfPresent; a non-optional Bool with a default does not.) So a stored {"key":"TOKEN"} with no isSecret throws.
Blast radius, confirmed: the throw happens inside try container.decodeIfPresent([Variable].self, forKey: .env) (:46) or .headers (:48) - decodeIfPresent only tolerates a MISSING key, it propagates any error from decoding a present one. That propagates out of MCPCustomServer.init(from:) (:39-49), which the OUTER array decode cannot skip, and MCPStore.load wraps the whole array decode in try?: if let data = try? Data(contentsOf: MCPPaths.customsURL), let list = try? JSONDecoder().decode([MCPCustomServer].self, from: data) { customs = list } (MCPStore.swift:245-249). On failure customs simply stays []. Every custom server disappears, silently, with no error surfaced anywhere.
The irony the source documents at :37-38 - "Decoded tolerantly: a definition saved before a field existed (or hand-edited) loads with the missing pieces empty rather than dropping the whole list" - holds for MCPCustomServer's own five decodeIfPresent fields (command, args, env, url, headers) but NOT for the three hard-required ones (id, name, kind, :41-43) and NOT for the nested Variable. The comment overpromises.
Note also custom-mcp.json is encoded with .prettyPrinted and .sortedKeys but NO date strategy (MCPStore.swift:271-276), whereas mcp.json uses .prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys AND .iso8601 dates (:262-269), matched by the .iso8601 decoder at :251-252.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must reproduce the failure mode: a variable object missing isSecret drops the entire customs list, and a missing id/name/kind does the same. If the port's deserializer defaults isSecret to false it will load files Droppy rejects, and a user moving between the two would see different sets of custom servers. Keep the ISO-8601 date strategy on mcp.json only, and sorted-keys pretty printing on both.

upstream_defects: MCPProxy.swift:118-131 + MCPStore.swift:26-28 + :286 - a port repick after the listener fails leaves every provider config written this launch pointing at the dead port. exportAll() runs synchronously right after start(), before the listener can report .failed, and nothing in the repick path re-runs MCPProviderConfig.writeAll (its only call site is MCPStore.swift:286). Agents launched in that session reach a closed port until some other action triggers exportAll.

MCPProxy.swift:387-392 - the SSE relay emits ONE chunked-transfer chunk PER BYTE: for try await byte in stream { var frame = Data("1\r\n".utf8); frame.append(byte); frame.append(Data("\r\n".utf8)); await send(connection, frame) }, and each frame is a separate awaited NWConnection.send. Every payload byte costs 6 bytes on the wire plus one async round trip. Functionally correct HTTP, pathologically slow for a streaming MCP server.

MCPProxy.swift:398-402 - the non-SSE path likewise accumulates the whole upstream body one byte at a time (for try await byte in stream { payload.append(byte) }) before sending anything, so there is no streaming and an O(n) per-byte await for large tool results.

MCPProxy.swift:260-282 - a request that ends early (isComplete or error) below its declared Content-Length has its TRUNCATED body relayed upstream with no error (:276-277). The 400/411/413 refusals do not cover this case.

MCPProxy.swift:369-380 - WWW-Authenticate is not copied back, so a 401 from an OAuth upstream reaches the client bare. Any client attempting RFC 9728 discovery through a proxy route cannot find the resource metadata.

MCPBridgeSource.swift:50-56, :76-152, :218-234 - the bridge never kills a spawned child. A server that hangs during initialize or tools/list is abandoned after CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 with console.error("droppy mcp: skipping " + server + ": " + ...) and its process lives for the whole lifetime of the Pi / Command Code host. Zero occurrences of kill, unref or SIGTERM in the file.
MCPBridgeSource.swift:218-232 - loadMCPTools connects servers strictly sequentially with await inside the loop, so N hung servers cost N * 15 seconds of startup.

MCPStore.swift:335-341 - on probe success, states[id] = .connected is written unconditionally while connectedAt/serverVersion/tools are written only if a connection row exists. Reachable via refresh(_:) after the row was removed: the card shows connected with a tool count, enabledServers excludes it (it requires connectedAt != nil, :43), no provider config gets it, and nothing is persisted.

MCPCustom.swift:15-19 + :46 :48 + MCPStore.swift:245-249 - MCPCustomServer.Variable uses the synthesized decoder, so a stored variable object missing "isSecret" throws keyNotFound; the throw escapes decodeIfPresent and the outer try? drops EVERY custom server silently. The doc comment at MCPCustom.swift:37-38 promises tolerance the nested type does not deliver.

MCPOAuth.swift:172 + :699-701 + MCPProxy.swift:355-361 - a token response without expires_in leaves no expires_at, accessToken then treats the session as never-expiring, and the proxy's "401 -> get token again and replay once" becomes a byte-identical retry that gets the same 401. There is no forced refresh anywhere.

MCPHub.swift:59 vs :78-97 - the failed set is read only by tools(). A server whose listTools threw is dropped from the tool list but is relaunched on any direct call(), because call() never consults failed and the toolCache guard is skipped when no cache entry exists.

MCPHub.swift:187 - initialized is cleared only by stop(), and the HTTP path has no restart or dead state at all (:421-452). An HTTP client whose remote session has been dropped keeps believing it is initialized until MCPStore.exportAll triggers reload().

MCPKeychain.swift:37-49 - SecItemUpdate's query carries no kSecAttrAccessible, so an item created by an earlier build keeps its original accessibility forever; only the SecItemAdd fallback applies kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked. Accessibility never migrates.

MCPOAuth.swift:815-821 - randomToken fills bytes with UInt8.random(in:), Swift's default RNG, rather than SecRandomCopyBytes. It is used for the PKCE verifier (32 bytes) and the CSRF state (24 bytes). Reproduce the sizes and base64url encoding; the port's RNG choice is its own decision but the byte counts are parity-relevant.

MCPProviderConfig.swift:10 :18 :34 :41 :59 :66 :131 :136 - a missing url or command becomes the EMPTY STRING in the emitted config rather than causing the entry to be skipped, so a malformed resolved server still produces a syntactically valid but unusable provider entry.

MCPProxy.swift:15 :23 :31 - proxy-port is never deleted by anything. A reinstall over an existing data folder reuses the previously chosen port, which is the collision the repick logic exists to paper over.

MCPProxy.swift:105 :117 :119 :313 - the proxy logs to stdout with print(), including "MCPProxy: listening on <port>", "MCPProxy: could not listen on <port>", "MCPProxy: listener on <port> failed: <error>" and "MCPProxy: request to '<id>' failed: <message>".
